sources.citation: Yul-Ifode, Shirley. 2003. Vowel harmony and vowel merger in Agoi. Studies in African Linguistics 32(1): 1-16. doi:10.32473/sal.v32i1.107348
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. The article covers only the vowel inventory (10 short / 7 long oral vowels), [expanded]-harmony and vowel merger; tone marks appear on the cited forms but neither tone nor stress/accent is mentioned anywhere in the text (grep for stress/accent/tone/pitch/prominence returns no hits).

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Benard Abraham, Fittokka Gobak & Longdi Sylvanus. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Deko-Dusanga [uya], Iyongiyong [bbs], and Robambami [ibm] Languages in Cross River State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-022. Dallas: SIL International. 64 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Sociolinguistic survey plus a 222-item wordlist; Appendix E (printed p. 44 / PDF p. 52) states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Section 4.3 'Robambami' (printed p. 6 / PDF p. 14) lists as prior linguistic work only the 1976 Ibadan student papers ('There is no reference to where the articles can be found'), Yul-Ifode 2003 on vowels, Dimmendaal 1978 and Blench's wordlists. sil.org is Cloudflare-gated from our machine; the PDF was pulled from the Wayback snapshot 20240908221…
